headline: A 45% volume surge over the past four weeks is landing well — today's 18 km easy run at HR 140 continues a pattern of aerobic efficiency improving alongside rising load.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The most meaningful signal right now is that you're absorbing a significant volume increase without apparent cardiac drift. Easy-run heart rate has dropped substantially across comparable efforts even as weekly distance has climbed — that combination suggests genuine aerobic adaptation rather than accumulation stress. The 4-week block is the strongest in recent history by volume, and today's session fits cleanly within that pattern.

The 20-week running streak is worth naming directly: you've matched your best-ever streak today. That's not a milestone to chase for its own sake, but it reflects a quality of consistency that is genuinely load-relevant — the base underneath the recent volume surge is real and continuous.

Strength work has kept pace with the endurance uptick, which matters for a training philosophy built on hybrid capacity. Seven sessions in four weeks is a solid cadence given the running load increase. The primary thing to monitor now is whether this volume plateau, consolidates, or you absorb another step up — the aerobic indicators suggest room exists, but a 45% block-on-block increase warrants watching recovery quality over the coming week.
watch_items: Monitor whether easy-run HR continues its downward trend or plateaus — a plateau here would signal the current load is being absorbed at ceiling rather than building further aerobic headroom.
Watch for any signs of accumulated fatigue in the back half of this week — a 45% volume jump followed by continued high-frequency running is where residual tiredness tends to surface with a delay.

Track whether strength quality (effort, feel, performance) holds steady over the next two sessions — this is often the first place load-related fatigue shows up in hybrid athletes before it registers in running metrics.
The streak is now at its all-time best — worth staying conscious of not letting streak preservation subtly override session quality or recovery decisions.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 181 km vs 125 km prior block (+45%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 145 bpm vs 157 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 9 vs 6 runs)
